pageCache.text:
Home
Come and see how at St Mary’s we do it differently!
We warmly invite you to come and visit our school so you are able to get a true sense of how we encourage our children to ‘Achieve their Ambitions.’
Please call the school to book a tour – 01273 418416
Welcome to St Mary’s Catholic Primary School
At St Mary Catholic Primary School, we seek to create a happy, family atmosphere where Christian values are upheld, not only in worship and Religious Education, but across the whole life of the school. Our school is a happy and thriving place, where children and adults work and learn together in a rewarding atmosphere, built on the foundation of enthusiasm, encouragement and high expectations. We work hard to achieve success and are fully committed to the development of every child in partnership with parents and carers and the community.
Our school is a learning school – everybody involved in the life of the school is an active learner. Every member of staff is totally committed to providing all our children with the very best education possible, where everyone feels valued, happy and ready to learn. We believe in a rich and diverse curriculum that offers a variety of real and memorable experiences that instill a lifelong love of learning.
This website has been designed to provide the school’s community, prospective parents and children with accurate and up to date information. We welcome visitors to our school at all times. I would encourage all parents thinking about sending their child to St Mary’s to book an appointment to meet my self, or if I am unavailable a member of our team, so that we can take you on a tour of the school. It is important that you see our staff and children in action and loving learning.
The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. To view our child protection policy please click here.
St Mary’s RC Primary School is part of the Sussex Coast Teaching School Alliance. Teaching schools help to raise standards by supporting other schools especially those in challenging circumstances. The Sussex Coast Teaching School Alliance, led by Benfield Primary School, will focus on six key areas: school-led initial teacher education (ITE); continuing professional development (CPD); supporting other schools (StSS); developing leadership (LD); specialist leaders in education (SLE) and research & development (R&D).Click here to be taken to their website.

Curriculum Drivers
Curriculum Drivers
Achieving Ambitions
Curriculum Drivers at St Mary’s
We guide our pupils on to the path to achieving their ambitions.
On their journey they Love one another, Learn to achieve excellence, Laugh through enriching experiences and Live life to the full.
We have identified four key drivers (see below) that at, St Mary’s, we feel are fundamental to the success of our curriculum and underpin everything we do.
– This broadens pupils’ possibilities and opportunities. High quality books and stories will be the main driver for the topics and curriculum. They will acquire rich vocabulary through a love of books that will enable them to express themselves confidently. The basic skills of reading, writing and mathematics entwined with our curriculum will ensure pupils acquire secure building blocks, which will equip them with essential life skills.
Diversity and Spirituality
– This helps pupils to be tolerant, respectful and value the differences in others. This will help them understand their role, rights and responsibilities as a citizen in the local and global community.
– This encourages pupils to have dreams and aspirations for the future inspired by inspiring role models and enriching opportunities.
Growth and Well-being
– This helps pupils develop confidence, motivation, self- belief and a strong sense of self-worth. They develop socially and emotionally and are being equipped to become independent thinkers and lead by example.
Curriculum Drivers

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Vision – St Mary's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Vision
Curriculum Vision
Our Curriculum Vision
‘Achieving Ambitions’
At St Mary’s, we want all children to achieve their ambitions and so from the moment they arrive in Reception to when they leave us in Year 6, they are on an exciting learning journey. This journey of discovery takes them to both real and imaginary places, where our children will become different types of learners including scientists, historians, mathematicians, authors and artists. Our children will learn and develop skills whilst exploring and discovering knowledge as part of each journey they are on.
The St Mary’s curriculum has been designed to ensure that pupils revisit and build on previously learnt knowledge. The curriculum has repeated themes, which come up time and time again in topics, helping children to assimilate new information and understand how this fits into their growing bank of knowledge. Through our coherent curriculum, children develop knowledge, understanding and skills, which ensure that they are able to maximise their learning potential. Children leaving St Mary’s do so having acquired academic, social and life skills, which will enable them to live life to the full and achieve excellence.
Curriculum Vision

pageCache.pageTitle: Smart Phone Free School – St Mary's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Smart Phone Free School
Smart Phone Free School
Our Smartphone-Free School Pledge
At St Mary’s, we are committed to creating a calm, safe and distraction-free environment where every child can learn, grow and thrive. As part of this commitment, we are a smartphone-free school. This means that smartphones and other internet-enabled devices, including smartwatches with communication or social media functions, should not be brought onto the school site.
Our decision is rooted in our mission to guide our pupils on to the path to achieve their ambitions. We want children to look up, engage with the world around them, build meaningful friendships and enjoy childhood, free from the pressures and distractions that smartphones can bring. By reducing screen-based distractions, we can better support children’s wellbeing, concentration, social development and safety.
Thank you for supporting us in helping our children develop healthy habits, strong relationships and a positive balance between technology and everyday life.
Learn more about our smart device policy below:
Smart Phone Free School

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors – St Mary's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Governors
Governors
Who We Are
We are a group of volunteers including parents, staff and the local authority.
Hannah Greaves – Chair
Sarah Clayton Siobhan Parsons
Folakemi Damola Lucy Parry
Current Governor Details
Former Governor Details
Business Pecuniary Interests
What we do
Governors are responsible for the strategic direction of the school and for maintaining high educational standards. We get involved in setting school policies, the admissions procedure, recruitment, school’s budget and improvement plan, setting targets and monitoring school performance.
St Mary’s is a church school (Voluntary Aided). The land and buildings are owned by the Diocese of Arundel and Brighton and the school is part of the Catholic Church. The Foundation Governors are appointed by the Bishop and have a particular responsibility for maintaining the Catholic ethos of the school. The governing body employs the staff, unlike community schools where the council is the employer. Governors are also responsible for admissions, rather than the council. 10% of the cost of all building improvements must be met from donations. Governors are responsible for collecting donations annually from parents and local parishes also make a contribution. Through the generosity of parents and the parish we were able to rebuild the Vale Road perimeter wall this year, improving security for the school. We were also able to replace faulty hot water boilers in classrooms.
Would you be interested in joining the Governing Body?
We welcome new volunteers to the Governing Body. Foundation governors are appointed by the Bishop and need to be practising Catholics and have the support of their parish priest. Parent Governors are elected by parents when a vacancy becomes available. The council appoints the local authority governor. We can also co-opt people with particular skills to become associate governors, so governors are not always appointed or elected.
We formally meet twice each half term and there are also other visits and meetings that you will have the opportunity to attend. The local authority and Diocese provide support and training for school governors. We are particularly interested in anyone who has professional skills that they can share with the Governing Body. Please contact the school office if you are interested in becoming one of the governors at St Mary’s.
To contact our governors you can email: HannahGreaves@stmarys.brighton-hove.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths – St Mary's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Maths
Maths
Subject Leader: Miss Savage
Our Curriculum Drivers
Intent
At St Mary’s, we offer a mastery approach in lessons, which enables pupils to become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics. They will develop conceptual understanding and make links between mathematical concepts. Pupils will have the ability to recall and apply knowledge rapidly and accurately in a range of contexts.
Implementation
At St Mary’s, we use the NCETM curriculum prioritisation materials to support our maths teaching throughout the school. We offer a mastery approach, using the curriculum prioritisation, to map out a clear progression for mathematics in our school. Teachers use the professional development materials to plan lessons within the sequence using a carefully designed pedagogical structure.
Concrete, Pictorial and Abstract (CPA)
Children and adults can find maths difficult because it is abstract. The CPA approach helps children learn new ideas and build on their existing knowledge by introducing abstract concepts in a more familiar and tangible way. The approach is firmly embedded in Inspire maths teaching.
Concrete is the “doing” stage, using concrete objects to model problems. Instead of the traditional method of maths teaching, where a teacher demonstrates how to solve a problem, the CPA approach brings concepts to life by allowing children to experience and handle physical objects themselves. Every new abstract concept is learned first with a “concrete” or physical experience.
For example, if a problem is about adding up four baskets of fruit, the children might first handle actual fruit before progressing to handling counters or cubes which are used to represent the fruit.
Pictorial is the “seeing” stage, using representations of the objects to model problems. This stage encourages children to make a mental connection between the physical object and abstract levels of understanding by drawing or looking at pictures, circles, diagrams or models which represent the objects in the problem.
Building or drawing a model makes it easier for children to grasp concepts they traditionally find more difficult, such as fractions, as it helps them visualise the problem and make it more accessible.
Abstract is the “symbolic” stage, where children are able to use abstract symbols to model problems.
Only once a child has demonstrated that they have a solid understanding of the “concrete” and “pictorial” representations of the problem, can the teacher introduce the more “abstract” concept, such as mathematical symbols. Children are introduced to the concept at a symbolic level, using only numbers, notation, and mathematical symbols, for example +, –, x, / to indicate addition, multiplication, or division.
Although we’ve presented CPA as three distinct stages, our teachers will go back and forth between each representation to reinforce concepts.
Our approach encourages teachers to vary the apparatus the children use in class, for example, one day they might use counters, another day they might use a ten frame. Likewise, children are encouraged to represent the day’s maths problem in a variety of ways, for example, drawing an array, a number bond diagram or a bar model. By systematically varying the apparatus and methods they use to solve a problem, we help children to make quicker mental connections between the concrete, pictorial and abstract phases.
When teaching young children their numbers, counters and multi-link cubes are more commonly used in the UK. But concrete apparatus is often put away by the time children reach KS2 because teachers consider their use too childish or distracting. By removing concrete materials from the children, they are being exposed to abstract concepts too early and are missing out on the opportunity to build the conceptual mathematical understanding which they need to take them through their education. This does not happen at St Mary’s as we believe the use of concrete resources is a must in our children’s learning.

Music
Music
Subject leader: Mrs Lelean
Our Curriculum Drivers
Intent
The National Curriculum for music aims to ensure that all children:
At St. Mary’s, we believe that music is an essential part of life and that the opportunity to engage in musical experiences is crucial for the development of the whole child. We inspire a love of learning through music.
Learning music develops all aspects of a child’s learning, from the physical action of using an instrument to the mathematical skills needed to keep a pulse. These abilities are directly transferable to other areas of the curriculum, allowing them to flourish and enjoy life in all its fullness. These skills will be invaluable in their future life.
At our school, children have access to music through weekly classroom music lessons and hymn practise sessions, as well as further opportunities to engage in peripatetic music lessons and extracurricular musical activities such as our choir.
We also endeavour to provide wider performance opportunities with other schools and in the local community.
Perform, listen to, review and evaluate music
Implementation
Our music curriculum is progressive throughout the school and ensures that children are given opportunity to sing, listen, play, perform and evaluate.
This is facilitated through weekly classroom music lessons, taught by a specialist music teacher, as well as through our weekly hymn practise sessions and a variety of concerts and performances throughout the academic year.
Throughout the school, children are taught to understand and explore how music is created, produced and communicated, including through the inter-related musical elements: pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture, structure and appropriate musical notations.
Our music programme provides children teaches children to perform, listen to, review and evaluate music across a range of historical periods, genres, styles and traditions, including the works of the great composers and musicians.
Children will also learn to sing and to use their voices appropriately and to create and compose music on their own and with others, as well as having the opportunity to learn a musical instrument and use music technology appropriately.

In KS2, children are taught to:

Impact
Throughout a child’s journey at St Mary’s, their musical skills and understanding are built upon year after year.
Benefits experienced, through a high standard of music teaching, include achievement, self-confidence, communication and creativity. Music will also develop an understanding of culture and history.
Children are taught to access music with a confidence and an appreciation.
Above all, St Mary’s endeavours to provide children with an enjoyable music education.
